text: In the pre-training phase, the system trains a supervised classification model using labeled source domain data.
Labeled speech samples from the source domain serve as the initial input features.
The source encoder processes these acoustic inputs to extract discriminative speaker representations.
These extracted features are passed into the classifier.
The classifier outputs the predicted speaker class labels, optimized via classification loss.
Next, the framework performs unsupervised adversarial discriminative domain adaptation.
Source domain samples are routed into the adaptation branch.
The pre-trained source encoder remains fixed, providing reference feature distributions.
Simultaneously, unlabeled target domain speech samples are introduced.
A dedicated target encoder learns an asymmetric mapping to adapt target representations into the source space.
A domain discriminator processes the encoded features from both domains in an adversarial game.
The discriminator outputs predicted domain labels, driving the target encoder to generate language-independent representations.
